result.title: Preface
result.summary:
City of Temple City, California 457 Deferred Compensation Plan Request for Proposals for Plan Administration and Record Keeping Services
RFP DISTRIBUTION DATE: June 17, 2020 at 4:00 PM (Pacific Time)
DUE DATE FOR QUESTIONS: June 29, 2020 at 4:00 PM (Pacific Time)
DUE DATE FOR RESPONSE SUBMISSION: July 13, 2020, 2020 at 4:00 PM (Pacific Time)
Important Notice: If you received this solicitation from any source other than the Plan Sponsor’s Consultant, you must request a copy directly from Hyas Group in order to receive answers as well as subsequent updates, amendments and/or other documents. Failure to contact the Consultant may result in the rejection of your offer.

result.title: 457 Plan Services RFP Overview and Process
result.summary: Temple City seeks proposals for administration, recordkeeping, education, communications, investment, and related services for its 457 Deferred Compensation Plans. Goals include better retirement outcomes; assessing plan competitiveness; integrated administration and reporting; suitable investments; improved participant and Director education; online tools and administrative support; pricing and consolidation options; transparent, lower fees; and an orderly transition if needed. The City currently uses investment revenue and revenue sharing, and is considering institutional non-revenue-sharing investments with explicit participant fees for fairer, clearer costs. Hyas Group and the Director will review compliant proposals; the Director holds fiduciary and administrative authority and monitors the Plan through regular meetings. The schedule is subject to change: RFP issued June 17, 2020; questions due June 29, with a July 2, 4 p.m. PST deadline also shown; responses to questions are listed as a milestone; proposals are due July 13 at 4 p.m. PST; finalist interviews are planned for the week of September 14. Firms may email questions to Audrey White at Hyas Group by the deadline; clarifications and updates will be emailed to firms recorded as receiving the RFP directly from the consultant.

result.title: Contacting City staff with questions or for information related to this RFP is prohibited and may disqualify your firm from consideration.
key_items: I. OVERVIEW; II. RFP TIMELINE AND PROCESS
result.summary: Contacting City staff about the RFP is prohibited and may disqualify a firm. Submit one electronic proposal by the Section II deadline to the specified consultant email, copying the second address; provide the Questionnaire in Word and the complete Exhibit Folder electronically. Firms are responsible for timely receipt; late proposals, changes, or withdrawals and fax submissions are rejected. RFP changes or interpretations are valid only through City-issued addenda; oral guidance has no legal effect, and firms may not benefit from errors or omissions. Firms bear all proposal-preparation costs, and proposals remain irrevocable for 90 days after submission. Submitted materials become City property and may be public; identify proprietary content, though confidentiality cannot be guaranteed where disclosure is legally required. The City may reject proposals, waive irregularities, negotiate with ranked firms in order, cancel the RFP, make partial awards, and request references or other data. Contract duration and pricing structures will be negotiated; the City may protect key response terms, and no commitment is binding until all parties execute a contract.

result.title: MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
result.summary: The City’s RFP requires firms to certify 11 minimum qualifications: five years’ governmental 457 experience and sole administration for at least five plans under $25 million; no front-/back-end charges or transfer/withdrawal penalties except specified investment provisions/fees; full disclosure of investment and service expenses/revenue; no promotion of unaffiliated products without written City approval; California and Temple City business qualification; self-directed brokerage; ability to continue existing loans; in-person City meeting attendance up to annually; regulatory compliance; and RFP terms retained in the contract unless waived in writing. Questions or requested changes must follow RFP procedures; waivers are not guaranteed. Proposals must include an authorized, two-page maximum cover letter, completed questionnaire in 10-point Calibri (50-page limit excluding cover and exhibits), and requested electronic exhibits; submissions may become part of the contract. Contact only the City’s consultant, Hyas Group; unauthorized City contact may disqualify. Insurance proof is due before award. The City has 40 eligible employees, biweekly payroll across two locations, and values at least two annual onsite education visits. Its plan has ICMA-RC and Voya (CalPERS), 46 participants and $1,894,729 in assets as of March 31, 2020; CalPERS alone offers Roth.

result.title: Proposal Requirements and Communications
result.summary: Proposals must include, in the specified order, a signed cover letter of no more than two pages confirming the firm meets or agrees to minimum qualifications and can provide the requested services; completed Questionnaire responses in 10-point Calibri, within the 50-page limit and any answer-box word limits, without unrequested materials; and a separate electronic exhibit folder for requested descriptions or samples. Incomplete proposals may be deemed non-responsive. The proposal and later enhancements or materials from the successful firm may be treated as one proposal and incorporated into the contract. All communications and RFP questions must go through the City’s designated consultant at Hyas Group; contacting the City without authorization may disqualify a bid. Proof of insurance is not due with the proposal but is required before contract award.

result.title: IV. PLAN INFORMATION AND BACKGROUND
result.summary: Proposals require a signed qualification and capability letter, completed Questionnaire within formatting and page/answer limits, and a separate electronic folder for requested exhibits; submissions may become contractual, communications must go through the designated consultant, and insurance proof is due before award. The City has 40 benefit-eligible employees, centralized biweekly payroll, and values twice-yearly on-site education. Its ICMA-RC/CalPERS plan had 46 participants and $1,894,729 in assets as of March 31, 2020; CalPERS is the sole Roth provider, under review. Vendor data cover 2017–2020 assets, accounts, contributions, distributions, cash flows, hardship activity, and investment allocations. Brokerage accounts/assets are zero; managed accounts are not offered. Guaranteed-withdrawal benefits report no assets or participants; PLUS Fund rates, assets, transfer terms, and unavailable loan data are listed. Education costs and meeting activity are reported. The section also describes proposal review, references, optional interviews, negotiations, award and contract approval, and the City’s right to change or cancel the solicitation.

nodes.title: Proposal Requirements and Plan Background
nodes.summary: Proposals must include, in order, a signed cover letter (maximum two pages) affirming minimum qualifications and service capability; complete Questionnaire responses in 10-point Calibri, within a 50-page limit excluding the cover letter and exhibits, following answer-box and word limits and avoiding unrequested materials; and a separate electronic exhibit folder for requested descriptions or samples. Submitted responses and materials may become part of the contract. Communications must go through the designated Hyas Group consultant; unauthorized City contact may disqualify a bid. Insurance proof is due before contract award, not with the proposal. The City has 40 benefit-eligible employees, centralized biweekly payroll (26 periods), and an internal timekeeping process. On-site education representatives are valued and expected at City Hall and Live Oak Park at least twice yearly. The plan is administered by ICMA-RC and Voya (CalPERS); as of March 31, 2020, it had 31 active and 15 inactive participants, 46 total, and $1,894,729 in assets. CalPERS is the sole Roth provider, a feature under review.

nodes.title: INSURANCE:
nodes.summary: Insurance documentation need not accompany the proposal but is required before the City awards the contract. The City has 40 benefit-eligible employees, paid biweekly through one centralized payroll system over 26 annual pay periods, using internal time-sheet and payroll processes. The recordkeeper is expected to visit City Hall and Live Oak Park at least twice yearly to provide in-person participant education and services, which are highly valued by the Director and participants. The plan is administered by ICMA-RC and Voya (CalPERS). As of March 31, 2020, it had 31 actively contributing and 15 non-active participants with balances (46 total) and $1,894,729 in assets; “Active Accounts” means currently contributing. CalPERS is the sole provider offering a Roth feature, which the Director regularly evaluates and which is addressed in the RFP.

result.title: VI. QUESTIONNAIRE
result.summary: Sets response rules: repeat and separate questions, answer concisely, provide requested exhibits, and observe page limits and order; required exhibits cover insurance ratings, SOC audits and controls, sample statements, fee disclosure, fund information, and transition plans. A asks about firm ownership, history, finances, insurance, adverse events, staffing, public-sector plans and assets, client wins/losses, and affiliations. B covers recordkeeping, contribution processing, investment and enrollment features, cybersecurity, and custody. C addresses advice, education, statements, technology, service centers, and service performance. D covers sponsor support, reporting, outsourced administration, loans, compliance, legal support, and communications. E examines stable-value and capital-preservation products, investment choices and fees, non-proprietary vehicles, and brokerage accounts. F requests transition plans, timing and protections, pricing, guarantees, fee collection, revenue sharing, and reporting. H requests current, former, and transitioned governmental 457-plan references and contact and plan details.

nodes.title: VI. QUESTIONNAIRE (intro)
nodes.summary: Questionnaire responses should be clear and concise. Yes/No questions need explanations only when requested; requested explanations should focus on key points. Tables may be recreated without exceeding the sample’s space. Repeat each question before its answer, and separate answers to multi-part questions. Provide requested descriptions or samples in a separate Exhibit Folder. The response is limited to 50 pages, excluding the cover letter and exhibits; follow the required order: cover letter (2-page limit), Sections A–F response (50-page limit), then only requested exhibits. The nine specified exhibits are: insurance rating agency report; SOC 1 and SOC 2 audit reports; control objective results; sample quarterly participant statement; fee disclosure; sample capital preservation fund fact sheet; list of proprietary and alliance funds; sample participant brokerage statement; and sample transition plan.

nodes.title: A. FIRM STRENGTH, EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS
nodes.summary: A firm qualification questionnaire requests the proposer’s primary RFP contact; founding and administration-service start dates; business structure, ownership, and subsidiaries; company and retirement-services revenues; insurance coverage and limits; pending or recent acquisitions, sales, mergers, ownership changes, bankruptcy, and insolvency; credit ratings and recent financial metrics; litigation, investigations, other adverse actions, and regulatory citations involving the firm, parent, representatives, or subcontractors. It also collects employee counts and defined-contribution plan usage, assets, managed-account adoption, and public-sector client assets and participants by plan type. Further tables classify 457, 401(a), 401(k), and healthcare trust clients by participant and asset-size bands, including plan assets and sole-provider status. The firm reports public-sector plans won and lost by asset size and year, including decisions not to rebid, and discloses organizational or industry affiliations, relationship duration, and any monetary contributions.

nodes.title: B. RECORD KEEPING, CYBER SECURITY AND CUSTODY
nodes.summary: The section requests details on the firm’s recordkeeping system, scale, technology, SOC reports, audit results, and sponsor audit rights; file formats, contribution deadlines, error reporting, and responsibility for correcting errors; investment menus, Roth 457 features, account allocations and options, deferral methods, and paperless enrollment and statements. It also covers cybersecurity controls for participant-data access and handling, backups, encryption, breaches, data-sharing vendors, audits, account authentication, breach monitoring, and reimbursement policies and limits. Finally, it asks who provides trustee and custodial services, the relationship’s duration, and the custodian’s coverage, limits, deductibles, and underwriters for specified insurance policies.

nodes.title: RECORD KEEPING:
nodes.summary: A recordkeeping, cybersecurity, and custody questionnaire asks the firm to describe its recordkeeping system (proprietary status, years in use, participant and plan counts, and server or mainframe basis); provide SOC 1/SOC 2 reports and recent audit control results, including exceptions; and state whether authorized Plan Sponsor representatives may conduct audits. It asks about required payroll and loan-data file formats, daily contribution-and-funding deadlines, participant error-reporting periods, and whether the firm will make participants or plans whole for errors, including dollar and time limits. It also covers tiered investment menus on paper and digital channels; Roth 457 deferrals and in-service conversions; separate traditional and Roth allocations, self-directed account options, and statement reporting; processing deferrals as percentages or dollar amounts; paperless enrollment and statements and their implementation requirements; and whether paperless statements can be the default.

nodes.summary: The questionnaire requests details on data-security processes, including access to current and archived participant data and controls over viewing, printing, or removing it; backup frequency and offsite locations; encryption in storage and transit; security breaches over the past three years and under the current system; external vendors or partners receiving participant information and what is shared; audit frequency, latest audit date, auditor, and findings; account protections (multifactor login, unique login, password-change frequency, and minimum length); third-party monitoring services after account breaches; and reimbursement policies and loss limits for cyber or fraudulent losses. It also asks who will provide trustee/custodial services and the relationship length, plus the custodian’s insurance policy limits, deductibles, and underwriters for errors and omissions, directors and officers, general liability, financial institution bond, cyber security, workers’ compensation, auto, and other coverage.

Also requests service-center locations, hours, staffing and licensing, plus 2016–2018 call-center and website performance, transaction-channel and turnover statistics.

nodes.title: ON-LINE ADVICE / MANAGED ACCOUNT SERVICES:
nodes.summary: The section asks whether the firm offers participants online investment advice and/or managed accounts and, if so, requests provider and service names, start date, public-sector participant and plan counts, assets, and average participant utilization per plan for each service. It also asks whether the sponsor may offer online advice without managed accounts; whether managed accounts can be limited to retirees and separated participants or tailored to retirees taking distributions; whether distributions can come from a specific investment option, such as Stable Value; whether assigned representatives will use the online advice tool to help participants select an allocation; whether the firm or its advice partner assumes fiduciary responsibility; and whether a separate contract with an advice partner is required.

nodes.title: COMMUNICATION AND EDUCATION:
nodes.summary: Covers whether on-site representatives provide one-on-one assistance with online investment advice, including annual meetings, hours, and whether those hours count toward participant education; required certifications, licenses, and training, distinguished by on-site and home-office staff; and on-site and call-center availability. It also addresses personnel disclosure events and provider disclosures, comprehensive financial planning and CFP qualifications, staffing and resources, representative profiles and work arrangements, schedules and response times, sponsor input on selection, and handling personnel concerns. The section requests education meeting commitments, service-day and education-hour allocations, compensation and incentives, and methods for measuring and quarterly reporting campaign effectiveness. It covers retirement-readiness tools across statements, web, and mobile; participant surveys, frequency, and cost; customized educational materials across channels; and webinars, including interactive sessions.

nodes.title: D. PLAN SPONSOR SERVICES
nodes.summary: The section gathers information on plan-sponsor services, including day-to-day representatives’ qualifications, experience, workload, service levels, relationship-manager arrangements, meetings, sponsor input and complaint handling; client-survey frequency and administration; sponsor staff access to participant data and ability to make changes; available reports, delivery frequency and paper/online access; and a sample sponsor website/mobile login. It asks which administrative tasks can be outsourced, what online services are available, and how the firm handles loans, defaults, separated employees, applications and repayments. It also requests public-sector loan-default, auto-enrollment and Roth-deferral data, and asks about catch-up contribution distinctions and other outsourcing. Further topics include communications and education compliance, Section 404(c), DOL fee disclosures for non-ERISA plans, indemnification for education claims, legal and regulatory support and notices, model plan documents, and sponsor newsletters.

nodes.title: Survey frequency: Internally or outsourced: Responsible for conducing survey:
nodes.summary: The section requests information about plan sponsor services. For up to two day-to-day representatives (excluding education representatives), provide name, tenure, location, accounts/assets/participants serviced, education, credentials and licenses, work schedule, and phone-call response time. Indicate whether the firm assigns a single-point-of-contact relationship manager, whether they attend sponsor-office meetings, whether the sponsor can help select them, and how dissatisfaction would be handled. Describe client-satisfaction survey frequency, whether surveys are internal or outsourced, and who conducts them. For authorized sponsor staff, report whether they can change participant information, record termination dates, view participant deferrals and dated balances, quarterly statements, and year-to-date contributions; specify format and when changes take effect. List report availability and frequency, including loans, payroll contributions, plan statements, cash flow, investment returns, lost addresses, eligibility, administrative allowance, transactions, and 408(b)(2) fee disclosure, with paper and website availability. Provide demo sponsor website/mobile address, login, password or security question, and expiration date.

nodes.title: Sample Website
nodes.summary: The questionnaire asks which plan-administration functions the firm can fully outsource, including QDROs, distributions, beneficiary changes, plan documents and loans; available online sponsor services; loan-default reporting and sponsor assistance; repayment after separation, applications and payroll deductions; and ACH-repaid loans for former employees. It requests public-sector data on untimely loan-default reporting, government DC-plan auto-enrollment and Roth-deferral rates for 2016–2019, whether sponsors must distinguish regular and catch-up contributions, and other outsourcing services. It also asks whether communications and education comply with applicable federal law and Section 404(c), whether DOL fee-disclosure rules apply to non-ERISA plans (with a sample if so), and whether the firm indemnifies sponsors for participant-education claims. Further questions cover legal and compliance support for current and future requirements, notice of actual or anticipated regulatory changes, model plan documents, and sponsor newsletters. Responses may require yes/no answers or brief explanations subject to word limits.

nodes.title: Sample Website (intro)
nodes.summary: The questionnaire asks which administrative functions the Plan Sponsor may outsource and whether the firm would perform them fully, including QDROs, distributions, beneficiary changes, plan documents, and loans. It requests internet-based sponsor services; how loan defaults are reported and what sponsor assistance is needed; post-separation repayment options; loan application and deduction processes; and whether the firm administers ACH-repaid loans for former employees. It also asks for public-sector plan loan-default incidents over five years, government DC-plan auto-enrollment and Roth-deferral percentages for 2016–2019, whether the sponsor must identify regular and catch-up contribution types, and any additional outsourcing services. Finally, it asks whether communications and education meet applicable federal law and whether the firm follows Section 404(c) requirements. Several responses require yes/no answers or brief descriptions with specified word limits.

nodes.summary: Asks how many public sector clients had participant loan defaults in the past five years that were not reported promptly, causing taxes to be paid in the wrong year; requests 2016–2019 percentages of government DC plans offering automatic enrollment and Roth deferrals; asks whether sponsors must identify regular, pre-retirement catch-up, and age-50+ catch-up contributions; and invites firms to list additional administrative outsourcing services.

nodes.title: Additional Outsourcing Services: (200 word limit)
nodes.summary: The questionnaire asks whether the firm’s communication and education services comply with applicable federal law; whether it follows Section 404(c) communication and education requirements for public-sector plans; and whether it applies DOL fee-disclosure rules to non-ERISA plans, providing a sample as Exhibit 5 if so. It asks whether the firm will indemnify the Plan Sponsor for claims arising from participant education (with an explanation if not), provide legal and compliance assistance for current and future Internal Revenue Code requirements, describe how it will notify the sponsor of actual or anticipated legal or regulatory changes, maintain model plan documents, and provide a plan sponsor newsletter. Responses are generally yes/no, with specified explanations or descriptions limited to 100 words.

nodes.title: E. INVESTMENT FLEXIBILITY
nodes.summary: This section evaluates capital-preservation and stable-value options, including proprietary-product requirements, pricing formulas and rates, historical returns and compliance/audit status, market-to-book measures, portfolio and wrap-provider details, liquidity, termination terms, and market-value adjustments. It asks for benchmarks, available non-revenue-sharing products, floors and contract terms, put-notice rules, trading and redemption restrictions and disclosures, fund-processing timelines, outside compensation, non-NSCC processing and fees, and an asset-class-organized investment-option and revenue-sharing report. Firms must describe recordkeeping capabilities and fees for non-proprietary investment vehicles, GMWB product costs, portability and TPA support, and recordkeeping for other providers’ products. SDBA questions cover availability and brokerage provider; tradable or restricted investments; asset limits and core-account minimums; transfers, trading restrictions and direct deferrals; Roth and pre-tax handling and reporting; and a sample participant statement.

nodes.title: Required Proprietary Product Name
nodes.summary: The section requests information on proposed capital preservation options: whether enhanced pricing requires a proprietary product and its name; the crediting-rate formula and current rate; quarterly net-of-fee returns for the past 10 years; whether returns are GIPS-compliant and audited; and market-to-book ratios (or equivalent adjustment factors) and net annualized crediting rates for 2008–2019. It also requests a recent portfolio-sector attribution sheet identifying wrap providers, plus provider details including additional wrap capacity, S&P rating, share of portfolio wrapped, and fee. Describe participant and plan sponsor liquidity (50 words each), and termination liquidity by product, including book- or market-value liquidation, in-kind securities, and put period. Finally, provide any market-value adjustment formula applicable to enhanced-pricing products.

nodes.title: Formula: (100 word limit)
nodes.summary: The questionnaire asks for the benchmark used to assess proposed capital-preservation options; ten available non-revenue-share stable value/capital-preservation products, with expense ratios, credit rates, and proprietary status; and any proposed stable value or fixed option’s floor rate and contract term. It asks whether advance put notice may be started and withdrawn without liquidation or charges; whether trade limits, short-term trading restrictions, and redemption fees apply, follow fund-company policies, and are disclosed to participants. It also requests fund addition/removal processing time, any scheduled windows or platform restrictions, compensation from fund companies outside revenue sharing and the number of such companies, and whether non-NSCC options can be processed and at what fee. Firms must provide an asset-class-organized Excel report (Exhibit 7) of proprietary and alliance options, including tickers, expense ratios, and revenue-sharing details, and indicate recordkeeping capability and any fees for non-proprietary commingled trusts, general accounts, separate accounts, and annuity/guaranteed-income products.

nodes.title: Fund Platform Services and Recordkeeping
nodes.summary: The page asks whether participants are notified when trades or transfers incur redemption fees; how many days fund additions or removals take and whether they follow a monthly, quarterly, or annual schedule; and what restrictions apply to adding funds. It asks whether the firm receives compensation from fund companies outside revenue-sharing agreements and how many companies provide it, whether the firm processes non-NSCC-eligible options and any associated fee, and whether it will provide an Excel list of proprietary and alliance investment options, segmented by asset class and including tickers, expense ratios, and available revenue-sharing details (Exhibit 7). It also requests Yes/No recordkeeping capabilities, and any additional fee, for non-proprietary commingled trusts, general accounts, separate accounts, and annuity or guaranteed retirement income products.

nodes.title: Additional Fee:
nodes.summary: The questionnaire asks whether participants are notified of redemption fees; the time to add or remove plan funds; whether changes follow a monthly, quarterly, or annual schedule; and restrictions on adding funds. It asks about compensation from fund companies outside revenue-sharing agreements and the number of such companies, and whether non-NSCC-eligible options are processed and at what additional fee. Firms must indicate whether they will provide an Excel list of proprietary and alliance investment options, segmented by asset class and including tickers, expense ratios, and revenue-share details (Exhibit 7). The form also asks which non-proprietary investment types can be record-kept and any fees; whether the firm offers GMWB products, their name and investment/insurance costs, portability, and third-party TPA arrangements; and whether it record-keeps other firms’ GMWBs. Finally, it asks about SDBA availability and brokerage provider, and whether stocks, bonds, ETFs, mutual funds, options, derivatives, and closed-end LPs can be traded or restricted.

nodes.title: F. TRANSITION
nodes.summary: Requests a one-page transition plan for a November 30, 2020 start, including historical transition volumes by asset size and year, transition duration and timing guarantees, dedicated team and experience, and transition-period onsite education and communications. It asks how systematic distributions, separated or retired employees, and emergency blackout withdrawals will be handled; blackout duration, prohibited transactions, time assets are out of market, and ability to transfer plan or brokerage assets in kind. The section also requests proposed fees across service categories, asset and participant pricing, contract terms, proprietary products, brokerage costs and revenue, advice and planning, administrative expenses, and other charges. It seeks performance benchmarks and financial guarantees, reporting, and prior payments for service failures. Fee administration questions cover revenue-sharing rebates and credits, sponsor-imposed fees, account and investment arrangements, transaction statements, fee caps and allocation methods, written revenue disclosures, hybrid fee collection, and detailed Plan Sponsor Admin Account reporting.

nodes.title: F. TRANSITION (intro)
nodes.summary: Section F requests a one-page transition plan (Exhibit 9) assuming a November 30, 2020 contract start. It asks for counts of plans transitioned from other providers, broken down by asset-size bands and years 2014–2019; minimum and typical transition duration; whether implementation timing is guaranteed; and whether a dedicated transition team will be provided, including members, roles, and prior plans transitioned from the current recordkeeper. The proposal must state transition-period onsite education/communication hours and days, and whether these are additional to Section C commitments, counting partial days proportionally. It also requests brief descriptions (each limited to 100 words) of handling systematic distributions, communicating with retired or separated employees, and emergency distribution requests during blackout. Finally, it asks the anticipated blackout duration on the provider’s system and the total blackout days.

nodes.title: G. Fees and Expenses Proposal
nodes.summary: Requests a provider’s proposed annual recordkeeping, administration, participant and sponsor services, and on-site education/counseling fees, both per participant and as a percentage of assets, with and without proprietary products. Pricing is requested for 5-, 7-, and 10-year terms, including willingness to price without a guaranteed extension; longer terms assume contract renewal and carry nonrenewal risk. The questionnaire asks whether SDBA assets count toward revenue requirements; termination terms; products excluded from revenue requirements; SDBA setup, maintenance, and trading fees; SDBA revenue, its inclusion in calculations, and participant credits; and whether sponsor-imposed administrative fees can apply to all assets, including SDBAs. It also requests financial-planning and investment-advice fees, who bears planning costs, online advice/managed-account fee schedules and revenue treatment, itemized non-asset-based participant and plan-sponsor administrative expenses, and any other service fees.

nodes.title: PERFORMANCE GUARANTEES
nodes.summary: The section asks respondents to specify performance benchmarks and dollars at risk for missing them across phone response and call returns, statement delivery and online posting, participant services and meetings, financial planning and participation/deferral-rate increases, transition timelines and deliverables, administration (contributions, withdrawals, rollovers, loans), report delivery, training, surveys and satisfaction, and overall service. It also asks whether benchmark-compliance reports will be provided to the plan sponsor and how often, and whether the provider has paid clients for failures to meet such guarantees in the past three years, including the number of payments.

nodes.title: FEE ADMINISTRATION
nodes.summary: The questionnaire asks whether the firm will rebate revenue sharing above contracted amounts and how often; collect and return sponsor-imposed asset-based fees, including their calculation and frequency; describe account and investment options, core-menu requirements, asset custody and access; and provide quarterly statements identifying transactions, cash flows, and dates. It also asks about implementing annual per-participant dollar caps, using revenue sharing to offset administrative fees, distributing revenue shares pro rata to participants quarterly, and applying fund-specific credits or charges. Additional items cover written disclosure of all investment- and service-related revenue, hybrid per-head and asset-based fee collection, minimum and maximum fee caps, and Plan Sponsor Admin Account reports provided monthly or at least quarterly with transaction details and descriptions.

nodes.title: H. REFERENCES
key_items: Current Governmental Client References; Former/Terminated Client References
nodes.summary: Requests references in three categories, with four governmental employers or plans in each: (1) current 457 Plan recordkeeping and administration clients with assets under $25 million; (2) former clients served within the past five years but not currently; and (3) governmental 457 plans under $25 million for which the firm completed an incoming asset and participant-data transition within the past three years. Contacts should have managerial or committee responsibilities for current and former plans, and direct transition involvement for transition references. For each reference, provide client name, contact name and title, phone number, email address, plan inception date, and total plan assets.
